desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Requirement | How it’s satisfied |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX A6000 | `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| **OS** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS | `ubuntu-2004-lts` image family |
| **Machine type** – 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM (adjustable) | `n1-standard-8` |
| **Zone** – `us-central1-a` (adjustable) | `us-central1-a` |
| **Billing & API** – Enabled automatically by the `gcloud` CLI | `gcloud` handles auth & billing |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does **not** use “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services. The equivalent service is Compute Engine.*  
> *Make sure you have the **Compute Engine API** enabled and that your project has a **GPU quota** for the `nvidia-tesla-a6000` type.*

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Authenticate (if you haven’t already)
gcloud auth login

# 2️⃣  Set your project
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"          # <-- replace with your project ID
ZONE="us-central1-a"                 # <-- replace with your preferred zone

# 3️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | VM will be migrated during maintenance |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional: run a script on first boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers) |
| `--scopes` | Full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU driver installation) |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic (optional) |

> **Optional**: If you want the instance to automatically install the NVIDIA driver on boot, create a `startup.sh` file with the following content and reference it as shown above:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl example)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a `curl` command that does the same thing.  
You’ll need a **service account key** (`service-account.json`) with the `roles/compute.admin` role.

```bash
# 1️⃣  Get an access token
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Define variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 3️⃣  Build the JSON payload
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
EOF

# 4️⃣  Make the API call
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Explanation

* **`machineType`** – points to the desired machine type.  
* **`accelerators`** – attaches one RTX A6000 GPU.  
* **`disks`** – boot disk from the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family.  
* **`metadata.startup-script`** – optional script that installs the NVIDIA driver on first boot.  
* **`tags`** – allows inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic (optional).  

---

## 3. Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| ✅ | Billing enabled |
| ✅ | `gcloud` installed & authenticated |
| ✅ | (Optional) Service account key for REST API |
| ✅ | (Optional) `startup.sh` for driver installation |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=${ZONE}
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. 🎉

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or number of GPUs to match your workload. Happy computing!
